correctness.rationale: The proof uses the exact valuation formula in Theorem 1.2 of the primary source. For p=3 the only nontrivial order is 2; for p=5 the orders are 2 and 4. Odd p-power divisors of q+1 or q^2+1 are at most half those even integers, and elementary exponent bounds then give p^v<q^a in every q>p case. The q=p case has valuation zero. Thus equality at the ceiling can only occur for q<p.

value.rationale: The claim resolves the first two odd-prime cases of an explicit structural conjecture and shows that its stronger condition (2), not merely the eventual global bound, holds identically there. The proof isolates why the cases p=3 and p=5 are tractable: the only nontrivial multiplicative orders are 2 and 4, permitting sharp local size bounds. Although a later theorem makes the global inequality unconditional, the structural verification remains a motivated refinement of the original conjecture.
